title: Ars artium sive Ars magna cabalistica (PH337)
shelf_note: A Latin manuscript of cabalistic arithmetic and combinatorics: gematria sums on Hebrew letters, 'Divisio Hebraica', cabalistic diagrams. It belongs on a Kabbalah or Christian-cabala shelf. No tradition or collection is given in the packet.
structure_note: No structure counts in the packet. The written page numbers are 44 (record 50), 9 (record 95) and 54 (record 140), so the numbering goes back from 44 to 9 and then up to 54. All three numbers are plainly readable in the hand, so this is not a misread. The manuscript seems to have separately numbered sections, or the leaves are bound or scanned out of order; it needs checking. The catalogue date '1566' looks doubtful: page 95 cites 'Esch. Mezareph. C. 5.', a text known through Knorr von Rosenroth's Kabbala Denudata (1677–84), so this copy is probably later 17th or 18th century (I7). None of the three pages has a translation.

book_verdict: A cabalistic-arithmetic manuscript in the right shelf, but the transcription cannot be trusted where it matters most: it turns Hebrew letters into invented Arabic numerals in a gematria passage, and it misreads the ratio numbers (336:28 as 36:15, 24:18 as 24:16) so the author's arithmetic looks wrong. The diagram page reads the facing leaf as marginalia, and none of the pages is translated.
